newsitem.title: USA: Debbie Reynolds Hotel files Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Debbie Reynolds Hotel files Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

text.p: The Debbie Reynolds Hotel and Casino in Las Vegas has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection after failing to sell the company.

"After careful consideration and with the advise of my counsel, we have decided that in order to protect the company, there is no other choice but to seek protection of the bankruptcy court," Debbie Reynolds said in a statement Tuesday.
The star of over 35 movies resigned as chairwoman July 3. She still owns 26 percent of the hotel's publicly traded stock. Her son, Todd Fisher, remains president of the company.

The 193 room hotel houses Reynolds' collection of Hollywood memorabilia, but it does not have a casino or slot machines. The chief attraction has been Reynolds' nightclub act, which she performs in the hotel's theatre.
"The problems that exist today have not diminshed my desire to remain entertaining and working in the exquisite showroom and lending my name to the overall property," Reynolds said.
The hotel is about a half block from the famed Las Vegas "Strip" of glitzy resorts and casinos. It has been open for five years.
In October last year, the hotel reached an agreement to be acquired by ILX Inc. for a total $16.8 million in cash, stock and debt assumption. But the sale could not be completed.
The hotel remains open during the bankruptcy proceedings.
Reynolds' movies include 1952's "Singin' in the Rain" and 1964's "The Unsinkable Molly Brown" for which she was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Actress. Her daughter is actress Carrie Fisher.
Shares of the company's stock were off about half a cent at 14 cents a share in late trading Tuesday on the Nasdaq bulletin board.
